trigger: commit e7cb7643 was pushed to origin without the mandated pipeline being run on it
summary: PROCESS VIOLATION: a commit changing a route response body and adding a raw sqlite3 acquire/release pair to a test fixture reached a remote branch with no governance run. Caught by the operator, not by the author, who had judged the diff docs-only.
classification_rationale: recorded as a ledger row because the ledger is the retrievable evidence store; the commit message narrates it but only forward, so e7cb7643 read in isolation shows no skipped control

trigger: the diff adds sqlite3_open/sqlite3_close with no ledger
summary: Resource Ledger omission for a new raw sqlite3* pair

trigger: any REQUIRE throw in the ExecHarness constructor after sqlite3_open
summary: Raw sqlite3* member leaked on the constructor-throw path, reintroducing a fixture leak this same file had already fixed with SqliteHandleGuard 200 lines above
classification_rationale: cpp-safety explicitly DECLINED to grant the manual-cleanup exception; per the standing rule the exception cannot be self-granted by the author, so that refusal is what settles it

trigger: operator rebuilds a daily or weekly schedule following the runbook
summary: The runbook's list of what does not survive a rebuild was a CLOSED enumeration and omitted the firing time, which re-anchors to the rebuild moment because the scheduler never reads time_of_day

trigger: a SQLITE_BUSY during the harness's approval-schema migration
summary: No busy_timeout on the second connection, so a failed migration left no schema and every 'no ticket minted' assertion passed vacuously

trigger: operator follows the runbook's instruction to park a rebuilt schedule
summary: The documented disable call used a JSON boolean; the route reads a STRING, so the body was ignored and the call ENABLED the schedule it was meant to park
classification_rationale: the remedy for the re-arming trap was itself a re-arming trap

trigger: an already-executed once schedule on the renamed definition
summary: A spent once schedule was indistinguishable in the inventory and would re-execute when rebuilt

trigger: renaming a definition carrying a weekly or monthly schedule
summary: 'Rebuild inside the window' is unachievable for weekly (must also hit the weekday) and impossible for monthly (flat 30-day period drifts off the calendar day permanently)

trigger: operator authors a schedule following instructions.md
summary: instructions.md and getting-started.md document time_of_day/day_of_week/day_of_month as functional while the scheduler reads none of them - the two published pages now contradicted each other and the code
classification_rationale: PRE-EXISTING product defect this branch exposed; corrected in the docs here and filed as #2746, which is the more consequential finding of the run

trigger: an auditor reconstructs change-management history from governance.d/ rather than commit prose
summary: The remedy run produced no ledger fragment, so the designated evidence store was silent about a skipped control that only commit prose recorded

trigger: a legacy reserved-id definition is executed repeatedly across a fleet
summary: The reserved-id denial has an audit row and a published SIEM token but no counter, so it cannot be alerted on or rated from Prometheus
classification_rationale: DEFERRED A THIRD TIME, deliberately and recorded as such: a new metric family is a published surface (name, labels, cardinality) and belongs in its own reviewed change rather than appended to a remedy commit at the end of this run. The reviewers' preferred home is yuzu_server_instruction_execute_denied_total{reason} in server.cpp's describe/pre-seed block. FILED as #2748 during the PR re-review round, after a reviewer noted a deferral with no issue number is unauditable.

trigger: operator reads 'a rebuild must copy the whole row' and tries to do it
summary: The shortened runbook still instructed a schedule rebuild the product cannot complete: GET /api/schedules exposes neither scope_expression nor requires_approval, so the two values whose absence causes an ungated fleet-wide dispatch cannot be read back at all
classification_rationale: resolved by withdrawing the rebuild instruction entirely rather than supplying more SQL - a definition with a schedule now has no rename procedure, which is the honest state until #2742/#2746 land

trigger: reading the 400's message and remediation after the runbook was shortened
summary: The API strings and their comment still prescribed the ordered rename procedure that had just been deleted from the note they cite
REGRESSION between remedy commits: the 'always comes back enabled and armed' warning was deleted while the rebuild advice it qualified stayed

trigger: an operator looking for a stalled `once` schedule using the documented signal
summary: The detection signal was inverted for `once`: a dropped occurrence zeroes next_execution_at AND increments execution_count, so it is indistinguishable from a successful run - the doc described the recurring symptom for every type

trigger: an operator disables a schedule following instructions.md
summary: The published disable example sends a JSON boolean, which the route ignores, so the documented call ENABLES the schedule - the same trap this branch removed from its own runbook, still live on a reference page
classification_rationale: doc corrected here; the underlying API shape filed as #2747
